variants.change: Delivery was attempted, the parcel was returned, and the final "Delivered" scan is at the shop's own address.
variants.label: accept
variants.source: Seller reads "Delivered" on the tracking and assumes the buyer has it, but the parcel was returned to sender after a failed attempt; forum-style, not a specific thread.
variants.why: The only delivery scan is to the seller's own ZIP, so there is no proof of delivery to the buyer and the buyer never got the item.

variants.change: The shop typed the street number wrong on the label; it was signed for by a stranger at that other address.
variants.label: accept
variants.source: Seller hand-wrote or retyped the label and swapped digits in the house number; the carrier delivered to the wrong building in the same ZIP; forum-style, not a specific thread.
variants.why: Seller Protection and a Visa 13.1 rebuttal need delivery to the address on the transaction, and the seller's own label shows it went elsewhere.

variants.change: The buyer says they moved out before the order and forgot to update the address; it was signed for at the address on the order.
variants.label: fight
variants.source: Seller shipped to the checkout address, USPS shows it delivered there, and the buyer opened a not-received case after forgetting to update their address; https://community.ebay.com/t5/Selling/Buyer-filed-item-not-received-case-after-they-realized-their/m-p/34072685
variants.why: Signed delivery to the exact address given with the payment is proof of delivery under Seller Protection and a 13.1 rebuttal; the wrong address was the buyer's error.

variants.change: No tracking, but the buyer left a 5-star review for this order on day 7 saying the vase was on their windowsill.
variants.label: fight
variants.source: Seller says a buyer left a glowing review and weeks later told the payment provider the item never arrived; forum-style, not a specific thread.
variants.why: Mastercard 4855 can be rebutted with documentation that the cardholder received the goods, and the buyer's own order-linked review is that evidence even without tracking.

variants.change: No tracking; the shop has a dated post office receipt and certificate of mailing, and replied to the buyer citing it.
variants.label: accept
variants.source: Seller has a post office receipt but no tracking, and asks whether that is enough to win a not-received claim; forum-style, not a specific thread.
variants.why: Proof of postage shows it was sent, not that it arrived; without a delivery record the seller can't meet the not-received burden.

variants.change: The buyer agreed in writing to keep the bowls for a $40.00 partial refund, which was sent, then disputed the full amount.
variants.label: fight
variants.source: Buyer accepts a partial refund to keep an item, then files a chargeback for the whole payment anyway; forum-style, not a specific thread.
variants.why: The listing disclosed the colour shift and the buyer settled in writing; the seller should show the agreement and the partial refund already paid.

variants.change: The buyer sent the bowls back; they reached the studio unused on day 14 and no refund has been sent.
variants.label: accept
variants.source: Seller had the item back from a return and was then hit with a chargeback on the same sale; https://community.ebay.com/t5/Selling/Buyer-returned-item-and-then-filed-a-chargeback/m-p/34397505
variants.why: The buyer followed the return policy and the seller holds the goods, so the money is owed; this is a credit-not-processed case the seller can't win.

variants.change: The studio packed an ash-white set instead of the tide-blue one; the buyer's photo shows white bowls.
variants.label: accept
variants.source: Buyer receives a different colourway from the one ordered, and the seller's "colours vary" note is the only defence; forum-style, not a specific thread.
variants.why: A colour-variation disclaimer covers variation within the listed glaze, not a different glaze, so the item is materially not as described.

variants.change: On the day of the dispute the buyer emailed that they didn't recognise the charge at first, have the plates, and asked the bank to drop it.
variants.label: fight
variants.source: Seller keeps getting 'buyer doesn't recognize charge' disputes, some from buyers who later realise the statement name was the shop; https://community.ebay.com/t5/Selling/Buyer-Doesn-t-Recognize-Charge/m-p/33837169

variants.why: Mastercard 4834 fails when the seller shows two separate transactions for separate goods, both delivered, and the buyer asked for both in writing.
